{{external|rs|rsc}} {{Has calculator|Calculator:Combat level|nogetext=1}} [[File:Combat.png|left]] A [[player]]'s, [[monster]]'s, or [[non-player character]]'s '''combat level''' indicates the difficulty in defeating them in [[combat]]. For some bosses and most monsters it is reflective of their actual stats as well. {{Listen|filename=Combat Level Up!.ogg|title=[[Combat Level Up!]]|desc=The music that plays when levelling up.}} Normally, [[aggressive]] non-player characters stop attacking you when you reach higher than double their combat level. There are exceptions, however - for example, almost any monsters, except for [[Rat|Rats]], in the [[Wilderness]] will be aggressive no matter what your combat level is. By default, monsters with a higher combat level than a player cannot be attacked by using a left mouse click, requiring a right click to select the ''attack monster'' option. So, to be able to attack a [[Blue dragon]] with combat level 111 with a simple left click, a player would need a combat level of at least 111. However, this behaviour can be changed in the controls section of the [[Settings]] tab by changing the "NPC 'Attack' Options" setting. All new players start out at combat level 3, and the maximum level for players in ''[[Old School RuneScape]]'' is level 126. Players will receive a combat level-up notification upon reaching a new combat level. This can be disabled in the [[Settings|game settings]]. ==Combat level requirements== * {{SCP|Minigame|[[Bounty Hunter]]}} requires a combat level of {{SCP|Combat|32}}, in addition to 12 hours of account play time * {{SCP|Minigame|[[Pest Control]]}} novice boat requires {{SCP|Combat|40}} * {{SCP|Minigame|[[Soul Wars]]}} requires {{SCP|Combat|40}} * {{SCP|Minigame|[[Pest Control]]}} minigame teleport requires {{SCP|Combat|40}} * {{SCP|Minigame|[[Pest Control]]}} intermediate boat requires {{SCP|Combat|70}} * {{SCP|Quest|[[Dream Mentor]]}} requires {{SCP|Combat|85}} * {{SCP|Minigame|[[Pest Control]]}} veteran boat requires {{SCP|Combat|100}} [[Slayer masters]], by default, have a combat level requirement to get certain Slayer tasks from them, although this combat level requirement can be waived by showing them a [[Slayer cape]]. Players can get more difficult tasks by asking the Slayer master to ignore combat level, though this does not bypass the minimum combat requirement to get a task from that master. * [[Mazchna]]/[[Achtryn]] requires {{SCP|Combat|20}} * [[Vannaka]] requires {{SCP|Combat|40}} * [[Chaeldar]] requires {{SCP|Combat|70}} * [[Konar quo Maten]] requires {{SCP|Combat|75}} * [[Nieve]]/[[Steve]] require {{SCP|Combat|85}} * [[Duradel]]/[[Kuradal]] require {{SCP|Combat|100}} (and {{SCP|Slayer|50}}) * [[Mortimer]] requires {{SCP|combat|100}} and {{SCP|slayer|70}} (or {{SCP|slayer|99}}) Some items also have a combat level requirement to equip: * The [[black mask]] requires {{SCP|Combat|40}} ==Calculating combat level== ===Simple steps to apply the formula=== # Take your [[Prayer]] level and divide it by two and round down (''for example, if your Prayer level is 43, dividing by two and rounding down gives you 21'') # Add this to your [[Hitpoints]] and [[Defence]] levels and divide the result by 4. This is your base combat level. (''For example, if your Hitpoints is 60, Defence is 70 and prayer is 43 you should end up with 37.75'') # Add your [[Strength]] and [[Attack]] levels together, if this total is at least 50% more than your highest level in [[Magic]] or [[Ranged]] this value will determine your combat level #* If it is not, instead use the value of the highest level between your [[Magic]] and [[Ranged]] skills multiplied by 1.5 (rounded down) # Multiply the applicable value by 0.325 and add the result your base combat level for your total combat level. ===Mathematics=== \begin{align} \text{Base} &= \frac{1}{4} \times \left(\text{Defence} + \text{Hitpoints} + \left\lfloor \text{Prayer} \times \frac{1}{2} \right\rfloor \right) \\ \text{Melee} &= \frac{13}{40} \times (\text{Attack} + \text{Strength}) \\ \text{Range} &= \frac{13}{40} \times \left\lfloor \text{Ranged} \times \frac{3}{2} \right\rfloor \\ \text{Mage} &= \frac{13}{40} \times \left\lfloor \text{Magic} \times \frac{3}{2} \right\rfloor \\ \text{Final} &= \lfloor \text{Base} + \textrm{max}(\text{Melee}, \text{Range}, \text{Mage}) \rfloor \end{align} ====Combined formulae==== \begin{align} \text{Melee Combat Level} &= \left\lfloor \text{Base + Melee} \right\rfloor = \left\lfloor \frac{1}{4} \times \left(\text{Defence} + \text{Hitpoints} + \left\lfloor \text{Prayer} \times \frac{1}{2} \right\rfloor \right) + \frac{13}{40} \times (\text{Attack} + \text{Strength}) \right\rfloor\\ \text{Ranged Combat Level} &= \left\lfloor \text{Base + Range}\right\rfloor = \left\lfloor \frac{1}{4} \times \left(\text{Defence} + \text{Hitpoints} + \left\lfloor \text{Prayer} \times \frac{1}{2} \right\rfloor \right) + \frac{13}{40} \times \left\lfloor \text{Ranged} \times \frac{3}{2} \right\rfloor \right\rfloor \\ \text{Magic Combat Level} &= \left\lfloor \text{Base + Mage}\right\rfloor = \left\lfloor \frac{1}{4} \times \left(\text{Defence} + \text{Hitpoints} + \left\lfloor \text{Prayer} \times \frac{1}{2} \right\rfloor \right) + \frac{13}{40} \times \left\lfloor \text{Magic} \times \frac{3}{2} \right\rfloor \right\rfloor \end{align} Looked at another way, the formulae above effectively describe the following: All accounts automatically get: * '''+0.25''' Combat level for every ''two'' levels in Prayer * '''+0.25''' Combat level for every level in Hitpoints * '''+0.25''' Combat level for every level in Defence Which is then combined with '''''one''''' of the below options which is automatically whichever one results in the highest combat level * '''+0.325''' Combat level for every level in Attack and Strength * '''+0.4875''' Combat level for every level in Magic * '''+0.4875''' Combat level for every level in Ranged
'''Notes''' * Melee-based combat level can be up to '''126.''' ** Once the average across your attack and strength is >75 your combat level will always be melee based * Ranged/Magic-based combat level can be up to '''109.''' ===Wiki combat calculator=== This calculator can be used to experiment how combat skills affect combat level. {{Calculator:Combat level}} ===Colours=== Combat levels that are different than your own display as a different colour. These colours range from ±10 of your combat level, from shades of green for levels that are slightly lower than the player's to red for levels slightly higher than the player's; 9 unique colours exist for this purpose. {| class="wikitable" !Level !Colour !Hex Code |- |≥ 10 |{{overhead|(level+10)|color=#ff0000|bg=#5d5447}} |#ff0000 |- |+9 |{{overhead|(level+9)|color=#ff3000|bg=#5d5447}} |rowspan=3|#ff3000 |- |+8 |{{overhead|(level+8)|color=#ff3000|bg=#5d5447}} |- |+7 |{{overhead|(level+7)|color=#ff3000|bg=#5d5447}} |- |+6 |{{overhead|(level+6)|color=#ff7000|bg=#5d5447}} |rowspan=3|#ff7000 |- |+5 |{{overhead|(level+5)|color=#ff7000|bg=#5d5447}} |- |+4 |{{overhead|(level+4)|color=#ff7000|bg=#5d5447}} |- |+3 |{{overhead|(level+3)|color=#ffb000|bg=#5d5447}} |rowspan=3|#ffb000 |- |+2 |{{overhead|(level+2)|color=#ffb000|bg=#5d5447}} |- |+1 |{{overhead|(level+1)|color=#ffb000|bg=#5d5447}} |- |±0 |{{overhead|(level±0)|color=#ffff00|bg=#5d5447}} |#ffff00 |- |-1 |{{overhead|(level-1)|color=#c0ff00|bg=#5d5447}} |rowspan=3|#c0ff00 |- |-2 |{{overhead|(level-2)|color=#c0ff00|bg=#5d5447}} |- |-3 |{{overhead|(level-3)|color=#c0ff00|bg=#5d5447}} |- |-4 |{{overhead|(level-4)|color=#80ff00|bg=#5d5447}} |rowspan=3|#80ff00 |- |-5 |{{overhead|(level-5)|color=#80ff00|bg=#5d5447}} |- |-6 |{{overhead|(level-6)|color=#80ff00|bg=#5d5447}} |- |-7 |{{overhead|(level-7)|color=#40ff00|bg=#5d5447}} |rowspan=3|#40ff00 |- |-8 |{{overhead|(level-8)|color=#40ff00|bg=#5d5447}} |- |-9 |{{overhead|(level-9)|color=#40ff00|bg=#5d5447}} |- |≤ -10 |{{overhead|(level-10)|color=#00ff00|bg=#5d5447}} |#00ff00 |} ==Exceptions== Some monsters do not have a combat level despite being attackable; these include, but are not limited to: *All [[Reanimation spells|reanimated]] monsters *[[Kolodion]] (excluding his final form) *[[Solus Dellagar]] *[[Evil creature]] *NPCs of [[Chambers of Xeric]] (with the exception of the [[Great Olm]]) ==Changes== {{Subject changes header}} {{Subject changes |date = 29 March 2023 |update = Bounty Hunter Rewards Beta & More |change = Players will now receive level up notifications and sound effects when they advance a combat level. }} {{Subject changes footer}} ==Trivia== *In ''[[RuneScape Classic]]'', the maximum combat level is 123 due to an alternative combat level formula. *In ''{{RSL|RuneScape}}'', the maximum combat level was increased from 126 to 138 in 2008 with the release of the {{RSL|Summoning}} skill. It was then further increased to 152 in 2023 with the release of the {{RSL|Necromancy}} combat style. The maximum levels of {{RSL|Attack}}, {{RSL|Strength}}, {{RSL|Ranged}} and {{RSL|Magic}} were also later increased to {{RSL|True skill mastery|120}} to match Necromancy's maximum level, however this had no impact on the maximum combat level due to how the formula is calculated.
